articles.title: Netflix may have finally figured out games
articles.summary: The new TV-based games feel right.
articles.body: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on Netflix, follow Andrew Webster. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started Boggle has become a spectator sport in my household. Everyone crowds around the TV while one of us plays, and the crowd either helps shout out words or waits patiently for their turn. There’s a lot of yelling. But it’s a game that my family can hop into easily, and once someone starts playing, it seems everyone slowly drifts into the room to join in. The surprising part is that the experience is happening entirely through Netflix. The streaming giant has been trying to crack gaming for half a decade now, and outside of a few rare hits like Grand Theft Auto and Squid Game: Unleashed, it hasn’t made much of a dent. But with its relatively new TV games, which launched last year and include the likes of Boggle as well as party games based on everything from Lego to Knives Out, Netflix may have finally figured out gaming that makes sense for the service. You don’t even need controllers: Each player just uses their own smartphone. As Netflix continues to expand beyond traditional TV and movie offerings, getting into everything from live sports to talent competitions with audience interaction, these kinds of games could eventually become a pillar of the service. And it all starts with Boggle. How it’s going It’s been a rough road to this point. Netflix first started rolling out games in 2021, and initially, it seemed like a great deal. Games are included as part of a regular subscription, and at first the service offered a nicely curated selection of mobile games. There were ports of beloved indie titles like the sci-fi strategy game Into the Breach, as well as exclusive titles like the exhilarating adventure Laya’s Horizon. These sat alongside games based on Netflix shows like The Queen’s Gambit and Love Is Blind. If you were looking for high-quality games for your phone, Netflix was a surprisingly great platform. The problem is that few people seemed to notice — early reports suggested that less than 1 percent of subscribers actually played games. This didn’t stop Netflix from trying. It invested heavily in the space, adding major games to the platform, acquiring developers, and at one point even trying to build a AAA level studio of its own. But there was no consistency, and the strategy shifted constantly. For instance, last year Netflix’s president of games Alain Tascan outlined four key pillars that would define the company’s gaming efforts, telling me that “we need to find our voice.” But there have been changes even since then. Two of the games highlighted during that event in 2025 were the battle royale Squid Game: Unleashed and the upcoming cozy MMO Spirit Crossing; since then Netflix shut down the studio behind Unleashed and Spirit Crossing developer Spry Fox bought itself out from Netflix in order to go independent. The streamer has thrown a lot of money at the gaming problem, but has mostly met with failure. That AAA studio shut down before it ever even released a game. Gaming is not an easy space to compete in. Other wealthy companies like Amazon have largely struggled to make headway, and even massively popular games like Fortnite are struggling. The issue with Netflix, though, is that its gaming efforts always felt separate from everything else it was doing. Hades on my phone is cool, but it’s also something I had to actively know about and search for. It’s not something I can stumble on while browsing Netflix, and it’s not something that will keep me in the main Netflix app, which is what the company wants. But the new TV games solve that issue. Before, Netflix’s games were separate apps you downloaded on your phone. Now they’re found in the same place as everything else on Netflix — there’s a tab at the top of the app alongside movies and television — making them seamlessly feel like part of the service. My family can watch Wake Up Dead Man and then immediately play a Knives Out–themed mystery game afterwards. Games are no longer a separate service Netflix operates, they’re just part of Netflix. What happens next The TV games appear to be off to a good start, but there are a few things that need to happen before they can truly become a core pillar of Netflix. For one thing, they need some variety. There’s a lot of potential to expand the offerings and reach different audiences. Netflix’s early lineup of TV games has mostly focused on family-friendly party games, but the company has also seen success with early narrative experiments like the choose-your-own-adventure Black Mirror spinoff Bandersnatch. The Stranger Things-esque adventure game Oxenfree is currently available on TVs (Netflix acquired Oxenfree developer Night School in 2021), which is a good first step at broadening the scope of available games. There’s plenty more room to grow. The games also need to be more widely available. Right now Netflix’s TV games are in something of a beta, as they’re available on some platforms — mostly smart TVs and streaming boxes — but not all. For instance, I can play games through Netflix on my Roku stick, but not my Apple TV. Making them a ubiquitous part of the platform, no matter what device you’re on, will be key. Most importantly, Netflix needs to stick with it. This won’t work if the company decides to change up its strategy yet again in a few months. It needs to give its subscribers time to realize that, hey, I can play games here too. The early years of Netflix games have been plagued with disorder, inconsistency, and a whole lot of throwing things against the wall to see if they’d stick. Something has finally stuck — now Netflix needs to build on it. By the way * Netflix isn’t the only subscription service changing up its offerings, as Apple Arcade has similarly been backing away from indie titles of late, despite once being a haven for premium-priced smartphone games. * And then there’s Microsoft and its Xbox Game Pass subscription service, which has also been going through changes, including a recent price cut (yes, a cut!) and the loss of some high-profile games. * While we don’t know how popular the TV games are, Stephen Totillo of Game File noted in April that Netflix’s controller app was topping the iOS charts. Read this * Last year’s launch of TV games was such a big deal that The New York Times wrote a splashy feature, in which Tascan said this about the service’s future: “if we are able to bring this more innovative, more approachable, frictionless experience, we will start having new partners.” * For a little more insight into how Netflix operates, here’s an interview I did with David Edery, cofounder of Spirit Crossing developer Spry Fox. * Keza MacDonald, games editor at The Guardian (and author of an excellent book about Nintendo), wrote a great ode to Netflix’s previous iteration of games, calling them the service’s “best-kept secret.”

articles.title: Ravens vs. Browns score, live updates: Lamar Jackson out with ankle injury, Tyler Huntley gets another start in AFC North clash
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson is out again for the Ravens in Sunday's AFC North clash.
articles.body: The Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns face off in their first of two meetings this season in Week 6, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland.The Ravens are off to a 4-1 start in 2026 under rookie head coach Jesse Minter and set to be without MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson for the second straight week as he recovers from an ankle injury. That puts Tyler "Snoop" Huntley in line for his second start of the season following last week's win over the Atlanta Falcons in overtime.The Browns have surprised so far this season with a 3-2 record, but are coming off a loss against the New York Jets last week. Deshaun Watson has thrown a touchdown pass in each of his starts this season. He did take a whopping eight sacks last week though, which may not bode well against the Ravens defense, which has delivered a 11.1% quarterback knockdown rate, good for 12th in the league.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Browns host the Ravens for their first meeting of the season in Week 6, airing on Fox.

articles.title: Rays vs. Guardians live updates, lineups, where to watch: Parker Messick, Drew Rasmussen to start Game 5 of ALCS
articles.summary: The ALCS is tied 2-2 heading into Game 5.
articles.body: The ALCS continues Sunday, as the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians face off in Game 5 at Progressive Field, with first pitch set for 5:08 p.m. ET. The ALCS is tied 2-2 heading into Game 5, with this set to be the last matchup in Cleveland before the series heads back to Tropicana Field. Sunday was originally scheduled to be an off day for the ALCS, but heavy rain forced Game 4 of the series to be postponed — so, we've got some (relatively) impromptu Sunday baseball! The Rays are set to start right-hander Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67 ERA), making his second start of the series. In Game 1, he struck out 7 while allowing 8 hits and 2 earned runs over six innings, with both runs coming on solo homers by Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey.The Guardians will start rookie left-hander Parker Messick (12-9, 2.56 ERA), also set to make his second start of the series. In Game 2, Messick tossed three scoreless innings before an error by All-Star José Ramírez opened the door for the Rays in the fourth. Tampa Bay scored three unearned runs in the inning, and Cleveland never recovered, dropping a 3-1 decision for its first loss of the series.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Guardians host the Rays in Game 5 of the ALCS, airing at 5:08 p.m. ET on TBS and truTV.

articles.title: Dak Prescott and Cowboys offense' were surprising no-shows as Packers get emphatic win
articles.summary: The Cowboys fell to 4-2 with the offense doing very little on Sunday night.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys might be in trouble. If the offense is going to be a problem, it's going to be a very long season in Dallas. After five games it was clear the Cowboys’ defense was an issue. It ranked near or at the bottom of the league in many key statistics. But the thought was the Cowboys could outscore enough opponents to remain afloat in a bad NFC East. The Cowboys’ defense showed improvement Sunday night at the Green Bay Packers, but the offense was horrible and the Cowboys lost their second straight game. Dak Prescott took plenty of punishment from a blitz-heavy game plan by Green Bay and the offense was stuck most of the night. There were no big plays and not many points. The Packers breezed their way to a 23-13 win. The Cowboys were stuck on seven points until a touchdown with 44 seconds left. Green Bay Packers' Evan Williams stops Dallas Cowboys' Dak Prescott during Sunday night's game. (AP Photo/Matt Ludtke)AP Photo/Matt LudtkeThe Packers have looked much better the last two weeks after a lukewarm start to the season. Their defense has played better and Jordan Love is on a hot streak. Love had a tremendous night, navigating regular pressure to generate big plays. The Packers are 4-2, which is a great start for them considering some of the early-season struggles. The Cowboys can't be as optimistic. They're 2-4 and after two straight troubling performances by the offense, their hole is becoming bigger. Cowboys shut out before halftimeIt had been a long time since the Cowboys had a first half as bad as Sunday night. Dallas hadn't been shut out in the first half since Week 9 of the 2021 season, but that streak ended Sunday night. It was the fourth longest streak of not being shut out in the first half, at 86 games, according to NBC.Two interceptions contributed to the Cowboys getting shut out before halftime. One came a play after Dak Prescott took a huge hit and stayed down for a few moments. The other was after CeeDee Lamb slipped planting his foot on a slant and rookie Brandon Cisse had an easy pick. The Packers led 17-0 and it could have been worse. Matthew Golden, who caught the first touchdown of the game, had two more touchdowns he couldn't haul in. One was a particularly bad drop on a perfect deep pass by Love that went through his hands. In the third quarter, Christian Watson had a dropped pass in the end zone on a nice throw from Love. The Packers left points on the board, but they still led by 17 points at the half because the Cowboys’ offense was uncharacteristically quiet. And Dallas wasn't much better in the second half. Packers slowly pull awayThe Cowboys’ defense wasn't bad on Sunday night, by its standard from the first five games. The Packers couldn't run the ball, though that's not unusual this season. There was a good amount of pressure on Love. After giving up 17 points in the first half, the Cowboys kept the Packers out of the end zone in the second half. The Cowboys expect to win when the defense plays at that level. On Sunday night it didn't matter because the offense was poor. There was constant pressure on Prescott. The Packers blitzed often and Dallas couldn't generate any big plays against it. Dallas didn't have a pass play longer than 17 yards until a 21-yard gain by George Pickens in the final two minutes, when Dallas trailed by 16. The Cowboys didn't have a run longer than 8 yards either. The Packers deserve credit for Dallas' issues. It seems Green Bay has figured some things out. It has looked like a different team the past two weeks. And star defensive end Micah Parsons will soon make his season debut after tearing his ACL late last season. Dallas needs to figure out both sides of the ball now. The defense showed some good signs for the first time this season but it will still be a work in progress. The offense wasn't expected to be an issue but it followed up a middling performance with a much worse game at Green Bay. A couple of weeks ago, the Packers looked like the team whose season might surprisingly go south early. They've made adjustments. Now it's the Cowboys who might be worried about where their season is headed.

images.caption: Green Bay Packers' Evan Williams stops Dallas Cowboys' Dak Prescott during Sunday night's game. (AP Photo/Matt Ludtke) (AP Photo/Matt Ludtke)

articles.title: Netflix se suma a La Velada de Ibai Llanos: anuncian una colaboración... ¿hasta 2029?
articles.standfirst: El streamer ha confirmado la colaboración en su cuenta de instagram
articles.summary: El streamer ha confirmado la colaboración en su cuenta de instagram
articles.body: No hace ni tres meses de que tuviera lugar la Velada del Año VI en el Estadio de la Cartuja. Pues bien, Ibai Llanos acaba de confirmar un movimiento que da mucha ilusión de cara a la próxima edición: la hará en colaboración con Netflix. Aún no es seguro cómo será, si la emitirá en directo en la plataforma, si podremos ver los combates resubidos allí o si directamente la empresa se encargará de realizar un documental sobre la misma. Es cierto que Netflix ya tiene experiencia emitiendo eventos de boxeo. Ocurrió por ejemplo en la velada que culminó con el combate entre Jake Paul y Mike Tyson, que según fuentes de la propia empresa llegó a los 108 millones de espectadores en directo. Ibai ha querido dar un paso adelante, y lo ha hecho con mucha fuerza. Tras dos años en La Cartuja, ahora se abre la opción de hacer algo mucho más grande. Netflix es una compañía que por sí misma ofrece mucha más fuerza que Twitch, aún haciendo que haya que pagar para ver el evento. Sin embargo, esta colaboración podría permitir a Ibai contar con muchos más recursos para la siguiente edición, y es verdad que aún no está confirmado que solo se vaya a poder ver en la plataforma indicada el evento. Todo lo que hemos conocido por el momento es un vídeo que Ibai ha colgado en sus cuentas de Instagram y X. En la primera solo lo acompañaba con un "La Velada x Netflix. Historia", pero en la segunda nos ha dado una pista interesante. El texto del post señala: "2027, 2028, 2029", una posible referencia a que la empresa se habría hecho con los derechos de las tres próximas ediciones. Podríamos tener, de ser así, confirmadas hasta La Velada del Año IX, algo que no nos podíamos esperar cuando comenzó en 2021, y que esperábamos seguir viendo surgir año tras año. Con esta colaboración, Ibai podría llevar el mayor evento de streamers de boxeo al siguiente nivel, y veremos qué está preparando. Ya en la pasada edición se habló de la posibilidad de contar con streamers que no fueran de habla hispana. El más sonado fue Marlon, que es uno de los más grandes del mundo actualmente, pero que indicó que Ibai le había ofrecido muy poco dinero. Con esta nueva colaboración, probablemente Ibai cuente con los recursos necesarios para ofrecerle lo que el creador de contenido quería, y desde luego la opción será mucho más apetecible para el estadounidense con Netflix detrás del evento. Esta colaboración podría dejarnos una Velada del Año totalmente increíble, por encima de lo que cabía esperar, y que podría durar hasta 2029 si hacemos caso al post del streamer vasco. Toda una locura.

articles.title: WNBA Finals: Dream tie series vs. Valkyries behind electric night from Angel Reese, dominant third quarter
articles.summary: Atlanta picked up its first Finals win in franchise history with a 14-point victory.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream have finally achieved a franchise first: winning a WNBA Finals game. The Dream bounced back to take a 79-65 Game 2 win against the Golden State Valkyries, thanks to the team's dominant third quarter and a stellar night from star forward Angel Reese.Reese, who scored 15 points in the first half, set the tone for Atlanta, and the rest of the team rose to her level. Reese finished with a game-high 30 points and had 16 rebounds, including 12 on defense.While the Dream ran away with it at the end, Game 2 was tight early. Neither team was able to pull more than a two-score lead throughout the entire first half and most of the third quarter.A 12-4 run from Atlanta to close out the second quarter gave the Dream a 39-37 lead at halftime. But they were in early foul trouble, with Rhyne Howard picking up four fouls in the first half, and Reese getting three.Even with the Dream on their heels, the Valkyries seemed in control throughout most of the first half. That changed completely after halftime as Atlanta surged in the third quarter, outscoring the Valkyries 21-9 by drawing fouls and taking advantage of Golden State's sloppy turnovers. Chase Center — affectionately known as "Ballhalla" — which was so rowdy during Game 1 and much of Game 2, went quiet.Angel Reese is FIRED UP 😤Reese comes away with the steal and brings the energy for Atlanta! 🗣️#WNBAonUSA 🏆 | Dream 💭 | Valkyries ⚔️ pic.twitter.com/WJfE1EsGJf— USA Sports (@usasports) October 20, 2026 The Valkyries needed a few minutes in the fourth quarter before they showed some life, but it wasn't enough to overcome the double-digit deficit.Monday saw a much cleaner team effort for the Dream than Game 1, as Allisha Gray and Jordin Canada dropped double digits and Atlanta stayed cool in booming Ballhalla. But the star of the show was Reese, who picked up multiple gritty and-one finishes in the paint and got fired up for her own plays and her teammates'.The second-half collapse was stunning for Golden State, whose shooting went quiet soon after halftime. Gabby Williams, Golden State's hero in Game 1, finished with 14 points, which led the team, along with Tiffany Hayes' 14 off the bench.But the Valkyries' real undoing was the fouls. The Dream scored 30 points off free throws after drawing 23 fouls. The Valkyries had 18 turnovers, though just four more than the Dream; 14 of the 18 were steals, as the Dream found ways to easily intercept weak passes. Howard had six of those steals, setting a WNBA Finals record.The Dream had been to three other WNBA Finals (2010, 2012, 2013), but were swept each time.Now, they're heading back to Atlanta with home-court advantage as they try to win the franchise's first WNBA title.

articles.title: WWE Raw results, grades (Oct. 19): Roman Reigns finally confronts the 946
articles.summary: Roman Reigns was in the building on Monday's "WWE Raw" for the first time since his title defense against LA Knight, and he finally faced down the 946.
articles.body: "WWE Raw" took place at San Diego's Pechanga Arena on Monday. Roman Reigns was in the building for the first time since his Money in the Bank title defense against LA Knight, and he finally faced down the 946.Family businessI have to say, it's nice to see Roman Reigns start to show he actually gives a damn about his family getting run over by cars and kidnapped. You would think he'd have sprung into action much sooner. Really, though, the Reigns' patience just highlights his heel ways.In the end, Reigns made the save to close Monday’s show after the 946 overcame the Usos and Solo Sikoa. It was built up with a dramatic staredown, and ultimately ended with Reigns hitting a Superman Punch and Spear to stand tall with his compadres.946 meet THE OTC!!! ☝️@WWERomanReigns pic.twitter.com/u2Hx8ZV5nk— WWE (@WWE) October 20, 2026 HERE WE GO 👊The Bloodline and 946 are FINALLY going at it!! pic.twitter.com/9rGUamtJ3L— WWE (@WWE) October 20, 2026 The interaction was fine, but it made one thing glaringly obvious: 946 needs to go over in this feud if we want to avoid a repeat of history. Remember when John Cena infamously buried the Nexus? After how 946 has been presented since their debut, they will desperately need the win in what will likely be their first full match together: WarGames.Does that lead to a Royce Keys title shot? Maybe. That could be fun. Where does Jacob Fatu fit back into all of this? Who knows. But it's relatively surprising that Reigns is taking his spot — at least that's how it seems for now. Don't be surprised if Fatu returns in the WarGames match, which only raises concerns about a potential Bloodline win.💼 Tease of the NightReigns bookended Monday’s "Raw," which is nice, considering how rarely he's around. But to start the show, he met WWE Champion Sami Zayn, who was all love and smiles, reminiscing about their days as part of the first iteration of The Bloodline. However, the tones of each man had intensified by the promo's end, with Zayn standing his ground as a continuously underestimated champion.It was a phenomenal interaction, despite its brevity. Reigns questioned whether Zayn would even make it to their Crown Jewel match as champion, a nice wrinkle that prompted the tease of Mr. Money in the Bank, Penta.Admittedly, it's pretty unfair to Penta that Reigns shows up to work so rarely, right? You can't be cashed in on if you aren't around. That's why Penta storming the ring in Riyadh to make a choice between the two world champions has some potential brilliance. Here's to hoping.The POWER that Penta holds!! 💼@PENTAELZEROM pic.twitter.com/ffj7E81r59— WWE (@WWE) October 20, 2026 BrokkenPenta's arrival wasn't just for the tease. He did wrestle Monday and picked up a win over Bron Breakker. It wasn't without your typical Judgment Day shenanigans, and the match was good, like every interaction between these two. But it really begs the question: What the hell is WWE doing with Breakker next?What a WIN for @PENTAELZEROM 😤 pic.twitter.com/89HebzP9RU— WWE (@WWE) October 20, 2026 Breakker's World Tag Team titles are exclusively a prop right now. There virtually isn't even a tag division on this show, so it doesn't matter. But guess what? There could be if WWE wanted there to be! So, that's insane. Get the belts away from The Vision — along with Breakker and Bronson Reed. The latter wasn't even on this show, and neither was Oba Femi nor Logan Paul. Breakker is already feeling completely lost again after the attempt at reheating him with the Femi mini-feud.🤡 Joke of the NightYou're probably wondering how this one isn't going to JD McDonagh vs. Joe Hendry, which is fair. But that's been a joke for a while now, so it expands beyond Monday.Anyway, before Lyra Valkyria's match against Lola Vice, WWE showed footage of Valkyria backstage earlier in the day. She was paranoid about being stalked by Bayley — which Bayley was indeed doing. Then she accidentally punched a passerby, Vice.It immediately highlighted how quickly this version of Valkyria has been turned into a joke, and her losing via a Bayley distraction (again) was so very apparent. Their blowoff "No DQ" match is, hopefully, next week, after Bayley announced it in the ring afterward.VICE CITY 🤩@lolavicewwe turns out Lyra's lights! pic.twitter.com/3LJ45gmdwh— WWE (@WWE) October 20, 2026 Valkyria should win so she can start salvaging her reputation. But I'm not sold. (Unless Bayley still hasn't signed a new WWE contract.)👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑Chad Gable is unstoppable.WWE announced pre-show that Gable would defend the Intercontinental title in a triple-threat against Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee, and you just knew we were in for a treat. He's already put on two absolute bangers with each guy, so combining the matches into one was guaranteed brilliance. And it was.TOTAL NONSTOP WRESTLING!! 🤌 pic.twitter.com/yMHNpvjDxa— WWE (@WWE) October 20, 2026 Gable ultimately came away the victor, as he should have — and now, we can hopefully move on from him interacting with luchadors for a long time.Listen, everything he's been doing with these guys has obviously been great. But we have to freshen it up before things get stale. (I'm not sure stale is possible here, but still.)Ethan Page and Big Cass each attacked post-match, which was a nice touch, since they could easily have been booked to ruin the match. WWE has been clearly focusing on giving the mid-card scene some serious love, so that's great. It's worth noting that Cass and Page didn't seem aligned, since they didn't interact. I don't exactly hate the idea of them working together, though. You have an easy team there, WWE. You're welcome.HORRIBLE 😨@OfficialEGO and Big Cass DESTROY all three competitors following the match! pic.twitter.com/2JNL9zHuJX— WWE (@WWE) October 20, 2026 I give Monday’s "Raw" a crown score of: 👑 6.5/10 👑WWE Raw full card results and match grades:Intercontinental Championship: Chad Gable (c.) def. Dragon Lee, Rey Mysterio — 👑 4.75/5 👑Lola Vice def. Lyra Valkyria — 👑 2.75/5 👑JD McDonagh def. Joe Hendry — 👑 1.5/5 👑Chelsea Green and Iyo Sky def. The Judgment Day (Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez) — 👑 3.5/5 👑Penta def. Bron Breakker — 👑 3.5/5 👑Recap "WWE Raw" with Uncrowned's live blog:

articles.title: Guardians’ Stephen Vogt delivers cold-blooded message to players after painful ALCS exit
articles.summary: The Cleveland Guardians’ postseason run ended with a 7-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night. How...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Guardians ' postseason run ended with a 7-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night. However, Guardians manager Stephen Vogt did not express anger or direct blame toward his players following the disappointing loss. Instead, Vogt delivered a cold-blooded message .

After the game, Vogt encouraged his players to embrace the disappointment rather than attempt to move past it too quickly.

'Let it hurt. Let it sink in. Let it fuel you this winter," Vogt said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Guardians entered the must-win matchup facing elimination after losing the previous two games of the series. Cleveland attempted to mount a late comeback, but the team ultimately could not overcome Tampa Bay's offensive production and timely pitching.

articles.title: Spotify launches paid podcast memberships with perks beyond bonus content | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Spotify's new paid memberships let podcasters offer fans exclusive perks, including ad-free listening, early access, and bonus content, while keeping 90% of the revenue.
articles.body:
Spotify on Tuesday launched paid memberships, a new way for podcasters to make money from their biggest fans beyond paywalled bonus episodes. Creators can decide which perks to offer listeners, which could be bonus audio or video, fewer ads, early access to shows, or some combination of these.

The streaming service first previewed the idea at its Investor Day in May, where it also introduced AI capabilities that let listeners ask questions about what they’re listening to or watching and debuted new tools for managing creator sponsorships.

As the company explained at the time, memberships would help to “create a natural path to go deeper, unlocking new and exclusive experiences for fans and new revenue opportunities for creators.”

The feature is now rolling out to 34 markets globally , including the U.S.

The launch is the latest example of Spotify’s effort to make its platform more attractive to podcast creators, particularly as it moves further into the video space to compete with YouTube. Though podcasters have long been able to monetize through ads, the new memberships could entice more fans to support creators by offering more than just an occasional bonus episode.

Creators keep 90% of the membership revenue and can package their benefits across multiple tiers and pricing options to appeal to fans at different levels of commitment. To qualify, podcasters must host their shows on Spotify for Creators or Megaphone, have at least 100 consumption hours, 100 listeners or viewers, and at least three published episodes.

Fans will see memberships promoted on the show’s Spotify page, where they can subscribe, pay, and immediately access the exclusive content. (The company tells us that memberships will be purchased on the web, not through in-app purchases).

A handful of shows will offer memberships at launch, including “The Adam Friedland Show,” “Making Sense with Sam Harris,” “Shawn Ryan Show,” “The Sculpt Society,” “Two Hot Takes,” as well as YMH Studios, which is bringing memberships to 12 shows across its network.

Memberships join other Spotify monetization tools, including advertising and the Spotify Partner Program, as well as features that help creators grow their audience, like promotions, free trials, and analytics. Soon, Spotify says creators will be able to offer fans membership badges and welcome clips, too.

articles.title: Streaming guide JustWatch becomes a streamer itself | TechCrunch
articles.summary: JustWatch, the popular streaming search guide used by 50 million people, is launching its own streaming service, offering free, ad-supported movies and shows alongside a $3.99-per-month ad-free tier and movie rentals.
articles.body:
JustWatch, a company offering a search engine and guide for streaming movies and TV shows, is now moving directly into the streaming business itself. On Tuesday, the company behind the popular guide that’s used by 50 million people is launching JustWatch TV. The new streaming service will feature content from 30 partners and will offer both free and paid tiers, as well as a movie rental store.

The media and entertainment company behind the streaming guide, the JustWatch Group, initially announced its plans to venture into streaming last month. At the time, it said partners like Paramount, New Regency, Fremantle, Bleecker Street, and Vortex Media were on board. The company has since announced other content partners, including Cineverse in the U.S., LEONINE Studios in Germany, SND in France, and Altitude in the U.K.

The 12-year-old company has long been known for its online guide to movies and TV. Essentially, it’s a “TV Guide” for the streaming era, helping users navigate a landscape where movies and shows move from one service to another, making it harder to keep up with what’s streaming where.

Available in 140 markets globally, the guide provides streaming options for more than 500,000 movies and shows across more than 1,500 service providers worldwide. This “where to watch” information and streaming chart data are also used to power some 1,400 partner websites and apps and are valuable to studios, distributors, streamers, and agencies that use the data to target their campaigns across social media platforms like Meta, YouTube, TikTok, and others.

Now the company believes there’s an even bigger opportunity to grow its audience data and insights by running its own service.

“At a time where there is so much choice, yet with so many people constantly searching for a place to find their favourite film, the series they just heard about, or something exciting that fits them, it is a great moment to be a hub for all things entertainment,” said Quentin Carbonell, JustWatch SVP of Global Content Acquisitions and Strategy, in an email shared with TechCrunch. “By having our own service with titles to watch directly on JustWatch TV, we can grow our already massive audience, while continuing to direct them to all our streaming partners. This is a natural continuation of our mission to contribute to the entire ecosystem, from the big screen to the small one.”

The new streaming service will be available within JustWatch’s existing apps and website across 12 markets, including the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Ireland, Germany, Austria, France, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Australia, and New Zealand.

Its free tier will offer a selection of ad-supported titles, while the ad-free version, JustWatch TV Plus, will offer more than 300 ad-free titles in the U.S., as well as other exclusive features, like advanced filters and the option to hide previously seen or disliked titles in the guide.

A movie rental store will also initially be available in the U.S., U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand, with more markets to follow in time.

While the ad-supported tier competes with free streamers like Tubi and Plex, the Plus tier will compete with low-cost streamers like Roku’s $2.99 per month ad-free service , Howdy. It will be similarly priced at $3.99 per month or $49.99 for a lifetime subscription. (The latter is an interesting way to price streaming, given the evolving content costs, but JustWatch believes there will be additional value in the data collected.) Paid subscribers will also be able to take 10% off on hundreds of rentals in the JustWatch TV Store, the company noted.

Like most low-cost services, JustWatch’s content lineup focuses on older movies and shows, as well as more indie content.

Another unique feature is that users will be able to influence the service’s content to some extent. JustWatch says users will be able to request titles they want to see to help shape what comes to the service.

articles.title: Netflix is telling investors not to worry, even though you’re watching less and less
articles.summary: Netflix said it’s making monetization a top priority as part of its Q3 2026 earnings report.
articles.body: Netflix is making monetization a top priority amid reports of falling viewing time. As part of its third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday, Netflix lists improvements to monetization as one of its main focuses going forward, alongside efforts to boost entertainment value and leverage new technology. The streaming giant doesn’t say exactly how it plans to improve its monetization, but the company notes that these goals will help Netflix “create member value that lets us occasionally raise prices, and increase advertiser demand.” Netflix also highlighted plans to push further into original titles, live events, and third-party programming as it faces an “intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention.” An analysis from financial firm Jefferies estimated that Netflix’s monthly viewing time per member dropped to 49 hours in the first half of this year, down from 66 hours in the first half of 2023, according to a report from Reuters. At the same time, Netflix made up 7.8 percent of US viewing time in the US in July, a one-percentage-point dip from the same time last year, The New York Times reports. During an earnings call, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos pointed to success abroad when answering a question about the company’s content strategy. “We see titles across Latin America, EMEA (Europe, the Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia-Pacific), driving engagement, subscriber growth, revenue, and profit,” Sarandos said. “Now, the US is also working. It’s just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we’d like.” Last week, Netflix laid off around 1,000 employees, while replacing key executives, including chief content officer Bela Bajaria and film head Dan Lin. Former Disney executive Peter Rice is taking over as chief content officer on October 26th. The Wall Street Journal recently reported that Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos complained internally that US-based users have been spending less time on the service, and that it’s “short on new hit shows.” In its letter to investors, Netflix mentions its upcoming lineup of NFL games, its Grand Theft Auto VI preview, and its partnership with French TV station TF1 as evidence of opening its platform to a wider breadth of content. The company reported earning $12.9 billion over the past few months, marking a 12 percent year-over-year increase. It also plans to bring its ad-supported tier — which raked in $1.5 billion last year — to 15 new countries in 2027. In the coming months, Netflix may be facing tougher competition from HBO Max and Paramount Plus following the Skydance megamerger, as co-CEO David Ellison has said that he plans to combine the two apps into a single service. The streamer struck deals with several creators as it competes with YouTube, which has reportedly offered channels “millions of dollars” not to post their videos on Netflix. Netflix has also weighed making even bigger changes to its app, including integrating other third-party streamers, such as Peacock and Fox One, as well as adding always-on channels, according to reports from The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal. Update, October 20th: Added a quote from Sarandos.

articles.title: YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button
articles.summary: YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos inside the three-dots submenu.
articles.body: YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, as reported by 9to5Google. At least two users on X have recently shared screenshots of the dislike button now being placed in the three-dots submenu, and a user on Reddit also shared an image of the dislike button being absent for them. Right now, for me, the dislike button sits right next to the like button under a video. Moving it to a submenu would make it considerably more of an effort to access, meaning that fewer people would likely use it. [Media: It’s unclear how widely this apparent test may be rolled out, and Google didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. YouTube has shown a willingness to make changes to the dislike button. In 2021, it hid the public dislike count on videos to help “protect creators from harassment,” though creators can still see dislike counts. Earlier this year, YouTube removed the dislike button from YouTube Shorts, suggesting instead that users take advantage of options in the three-dots menu.

articles.title: 76ers spoil Knicks' ring night in LeBron James' and Jaylen Brown's Philadelphia debut
articles.summary: The Knicks left Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night with rings. But the 76ers walked away with the win
articles.body: The New York Knicks left Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night with rings. But the Philadelphia 76ers walked away with the win.The 76ers capitalized on a sloppy third quarter from the Knicks and took control for a 106-100 win in the season debut for both teams.The win for Philadelphia arrived in the highly anticipated 76ers debuts for LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. And it spoiled a night of celebration in New York in which the Knicks raised their first championship banner since 1973 and handed out rings.With the win, the 76ers joined the Pistons in victory on the NBA's opening day after Detroit beat the Boston Celtics in a Tuesday matinee. Both teams fired early salvos in what projects as a competitive race at the top of the Eastern Conference.LeBron James and Jaylen Brown helped deliver a win in their 76ers debut.IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERSKnicks start strong, but 76ers take over lateThe Knicks appeared prepared to avoid the dreaded ring-night hangover and entered halftime with a 58-54 lead. But James and Brown found their rhythm in the third quarter to help the 76ers seize control.James converted two straight turnovers by Karl-Anthony Towns into easy buckets at the rim, including an alley-oop dunk on a pass from Brown.JAYLEN BROWN LOB TO LEBRON JAMESFIRST OF MANY. 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/CkjHSvPh3D— Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) October 21, 2026 The 76ers capped a 29-18 third-quarter advantage with a buzzer-beating 3 from Brown on an inbounds pass from James. JAYLEN BROWN AT THE BUZZERTHE SIXERS ARE COOKING 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4IUjWmQtaE— NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) October 21, 2026 It was a welcome sight for 76ers fans eager to see the first glimpse of Philadelphia's revamped roster.With that bucket, the 76ers entered the fourth quarter with an 83-76 advantage. The Knicks kept things competitive down the stretch, but never reclaimed the lead. First glimpse at new-look 76ersJames filled up the box score while taking a backseat in scoring with 14 points, 9 rebounds, 7 assists, 1 steal and 1 block. He struggled with his shot on a 5-of-13 shooting night, but, as usual, found his path to making an impact on the game.Brown also contributed across the board with 19 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists, 1 steal and 1 block. Philadelphia's resident All-Stars, meanwhile, filled their roles well.Tyrese Maxey led all scorers with 28 points in a productive night that also featured 5 assists, 4 rebounds, 3 steals and 3 blocks. He set the tone for his scoring night with back-to-back 3s to open the game. Back-to-Back threes from Tyrese Maxey to kick off the Sixers season 🔥pic.twitter.com/ZkY0iWCP1l ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 20, 2026 Joel Embiid struggled from the field while shooting 4 of 15. But he also made an impact on both sides of the floor with 13 points, 11 rebounds, 6 assists, 3 blocks and 2 steals.On a night when the 76ers shot just 41.6% from the field and 27.5% from 3, they found a way to grind out a win that Philadelphia fans can surely appreciate while leaving them excited for more. Ring-night hangover?The Knicks, meanwhile, looked like a team that may have not been completely focused. Towns played just six minutes in the first half after getting into early foul trouble. He finished with 19 points and 12 rebounds in 23 minutes. OG Anunoby missed all six of his first-half 3-pointers. He shot 1 of 9 from 3 and 3 of 12 from the field for the game en route to 10 points. And Finals MVP Jalen Brunson struggled on a 6-of-19 shooting night en route to a team-high 21 points alongside 5 rebounds and 3 assists. It was new arrival Andre Drummond who impressed the most. With Towns relegated to the bench for much of the game, Drummond anchored the post with 12 points, 14 rebounds and 2 blocks. He looks ready to fill in the void left by Mitchell Robinson, who now plays for the rival Celtics. The 76ers have one night off before hosting James' former Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday. The Knicks will visit the Celtics on Friday in another clash of Eastern Conference hopefuls.

images.caption: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown helped deliver a win in their 76ers debut. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS)

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns delivers reality check on Knicks after loss to 76ers
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns assessed the team’s shortcomings after Tuesday’s 106-100 season-opening loss to the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Squ...
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns assessed the team's shortcomings after Tuesday's 106-100 season-opening loss to the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden.

The defending NBA champions raised their title banner and received championship rings before tipoff, but the 76ers spoiled the festivities. The Knicks led 58-54 at halftime before Philadelphia seized control in the third quarter.

Towns, who finished with 19 points and 12 rebounds, pointed to the deficit his team faced and cautioned against expecting the same late-game execution that fueled last season's championship run.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

ClutchPoints took to X, formerly Twitter, to share video of the center speaking about the loss in a postgame interview. The clip, credited to SportsCenter, captured his blunt assessment of where New York stands entering another season.

"I just thought that we put ourselves too much in a deficit, and you know we're not that Knick team yet from last year."

The 76ers outscored the Knicks 29-18 in the third quarter, turning a four-point halftime deficit into an 83-76 advantage. Although New York won the fourth quarter, 24-23, the Knicks could not erase the gap.

Towns connected on a three-pointer with 4:37 remaining to bring his team within one point. However, the Knicks scored on just two of their final eight possessions, allowing Philadelphia to hold on for the victory.

Jalen Brunson led the Knicks with 21 points, while Tyrese Maxey dropped a game-high 28 for the 76ers. Towns recorded his double-double in 24 minutes as New York opened the 2026-27 campaign at 0-1.

Towns explained that last season's team developed its spark and execution over time. His comments reflected concern that the Knicks were relying too early on their championship-level execution before rediscovering that same consistency.

Philadelphia improved to 1-0, spoiling a night devoted to the Knicks' championship celebration. For New York, the opener underscored Towns' point that last season's late-game reliability cannot simply be assumed at the start of a new campaign.

articles.title: YouTube has a new way to protect hacked channels.
articles.summary:
When unusual activity is detected on an account, the platform will now temporarily pause features for 24 hours, including uploading or updating videos, livestreaming, creating or adjusting playlists, uploading thumbnails, and making private videos public. Full feature access will be restored once the account’s security is verified.

articles.title: Dasara: Cops rescue 4 caged Palapittas
articles.summary: Hyderabad police rescued four caged Palapittas (Indian Rollers), Telangana’s state bird, on Dasara and handed them to forest officials; action initiated.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Police have rescued four Indian Rollers (’Palapitta’), the state bird of Telangana, which were kept captive in cages near places of worship and handed them over to forest department officials.Acting on specific information from locals, Hyderabad police raided three places on Dasara day. Two birds were found in cramped cages near a place of worship at Bapu Ghat in Langar Houz. They were handed over to forest officials at KBR Park. A third bird was found in a cage hung from a tree near a place of worship at Chatrinaka, while a fourth bird was in a cage near another place of worship at Balaji Nagar, Mangalhat. They too were handed over to the forest department officials.Hyderabad police commissioner VC Sajjanar has warned that harming the state bird would invite strict legal action. He said action was now being initiated against those responsible, in coordination with the forest department.Some people believe that sighting of ‘Palapitta’ on Dasara day brings good fortune. “Caging a helpless bird does no good to anyone. articles.title: YouTube says it isn’t testing hiding the dislike button
articles.summary: A YouTube spokesperson, in a Wednesday statement to The Verge, confirmed that YouTube is “not testing hiding the dislike button on YouTube for users.”
articles.body: On Tuesday, I published a story about how YouTube appeared to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, with at least two users on X sharing screenshots of the dislike button moved into the three-dot menu. But a YouTube spokesperson, in a Wednesday statement to The Verge, confirmed that YouTube is “not testing hiding the dislike button on YouTube for users.” However, YouTube is introducing a new UI for creators on their uploaded videos where the dislike button will be moved. Here’s the full statement, from spokesperson Kimberly Taylor: > We are not testing hiding the dislike button on YouTube for users. We’re introducing a new UI for creators on their own uploaded videos, where dislike is behind the three-dot menu, and as always, they can find their full dislike counts in Studio, alongside other analytics. The new UI is rolling out to creators in “the coming weeks,” Taylor says. The change for creators follows past adjustments to the dislike button on the platform. YouTube hid the public dislike count on videos starting in 2021 as a way to prevent harassment, and it removed the dislike button video from Shorts earlier this year. Update, October 21st: Added context about the UI rollout timing from Taylor.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Dream roll past Valkyries in Game 3 to take a 2-1 WNBA Finals lead in front of sold-out crowd
articles.summary: The Dream made the most of their move to State Farm Arena on Wednesday night.
articles.body: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream took full advantage of their move to State Farm Arena on Wednesday night.The Dream, in front of a sold-out crowd at the Hawks' arena, rolled to a blowout 97-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. That gave them a 2-1 lead in the series entering Game 4 on Saturday. Reese, after dropping 30 points in Game 2 on Monday, recorded yet another double-double with 21 points and 12 rebounds in the win.With a double-double in each of the three Finals games so far, the 24-year-old is the youngest player in WNBA history to drop three-straight double-doubles in the championship series."We fought for this arena, so we have to protect it," Dream star Rhyne Howard said on the court after the win. "I think it's big. We went and stole one, but we couldn't let them come in and do the same thing."Wednesday's contest got off to an incredibly slow and historically bad start. The two teams combined to shoot just 3-of-20 from the field in the opening minutes, and the Valkyries missed their first eight shots of the night. Their scoring drought, which lasted nearly five full minutes, was the second-longest scoring drought to open a WNBA Finals game in league history, according to Elias. But despite that — and a stretch in which Naz Hamilton and Reese drilled a trio of 3-pointers in a roughly 90-second span — the Valkyries managed to keep the game within single digits at the end of the quarter. The pace picked up after that, and the Valkyries climbed right back into the game after falling down by 10 points briefly in the second quarter. A 3-pointer from Cecilia Zandalasini, the team's eighth in the first 20 minutes, cut the game to just six points at the break.The Valkyries came storming out of halftime ready to make a move, too, and even tied the game back up just moments into the third quarter. But that was as close as they got to taking the lead. The Dream rattled off a quick 8-0 burst, capped by a coast-to-coast layup from Reese, to take control of the game right back. A post with guard skills ✨Angel Reese caps off a 8-0 run by ATL by taking it coast-to-coast in transition to force the timeout call pic.twitter.com/gucDY95TAG— WNBA (@WNBA) October 22, 2026 They ended up closing the period on an extended 22-8 run while limiting the Valkyries to just three made field goals the rest of the way to blow the game wide open. Reese even sat out the final three-and-a-half minutes of the quarter, and the Dream still added 10 points with her watching from the sidelines.Howard pushed the Dream's lead to 20 minutes into the fourth quarter, and that was more than enough to seal the deal. They cruised the rest of the way to secure the 16-point win and take the 3-1 advantage in the series.Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 15 points and eight assists. Zandalasini added 13 points, and was the only other starter to hit double figures. The Valkyries are in just their second season in the league after joining as an expansion franchise in 2025, and are making their first WNBA Finals appearance.Howard added 16 points and four assists to go with Reese's double-double for the Dream. She had five steals, too, which made her the first player in WNBA Finals history to have at least five in consecutive games. Hamilton added 15 points, and Jordin Canada finished with 10 points and eight assists. The Dream are now in their fourth WNBA Finals since entering the league in 2008, but the team has never lifted a championship trophy. Wednesday night's game was their first Finals win on a home court, too, after they were swept the previous three times when the WNBA Finals was a best-of-three series. The series was adjusted and moved from the Gateway Center, a 3,500-seat arena where the Dream usually play, last week to accommodate the massive demand from fans. The 17,000 that showed up on Wednesday clearly had a great time.The vibes are high in State Farm Arena right now pic.twitter.com/Ezl1iFZChY— Alexa Philippou (@alexaphilippou) October 22, 2026 Despite the blowout win, this series is far from over. Thanks to the Valkyries' Game 1 win, the series will shift back to the Bay Area for at least Game 5 next week, regardless of what happens Saturday. But Wednesday night was a huge statement win for Reese and the Dream. And the energy that was brought to State Farm Arena is sure to show up again this weekend.

articles.title: Spotify's current AI bet is about being the music service that agents choose | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Spotify co-CEO Gustav Söderström explains why the rise of AI agents could be good news for the music service.
articles.body:
Spotify had a strong third quarter , reaching 788 million monthly active users and generating nearly €5 billion (around $5.6 billion USD) in revenue. But the more interesting takeaway from its earnings call was how the company sees people listening to music in the future, and why the rise of AI agents could be good news for its business.

Co-CEO Gustav Söderström thinks the music streaming giant is particularly well-suited to this shift.

“Spotify is in one of the few categories that actually stands to thrive in the agentic age,” Söderström tells investors. “This is because agents excel at replacing and taking care of things people would rather not do. People love getting rid of chores. But entertainment is the opposite. Nobody asks an agent to ‘summarize a song’ for them.”

Instead of opening Spotify, searching for an artist, and building a playlist themselves, listeners could ask an AI assistant to do the work for them. They might want music for a run, a podcast about something they’ve been discussing with an AI, or an audiobook recap that picks up exactly where they left off.

Spotify wants to be the service those agents turn to, letting people discover music and interact with Spotify through conversations rather than just its own app. Notably, Spotify was the first music service to integrate with Meta’s Muse assistant , and it also integrates with ChatGPT and Claude.

“Our goal is to be the media service that you use from any agent, really turning the growth of agents into a tailwind rather than a headwind. That is exactly what we are seeing now. We are seeing really good adoption of Spotify inside these agents. While other companies are maybe trying to figure out what to do and many are leaning out, we are actually leaning in and participating in the growth instead of standing by the roadside and looking at it,” said Söderström.

The market is already showing signs of friction over how agents access third-party services. Amazon , for example, has blocked Meta’s Muse from shopping on its platform, illustrating how major players may restrict outside agents when questions arise around access, security, privacy, or commercial control.

Spotify’s pitch isn’t just that AI should just make entertainment easier to find. It should make the experience more personal, too.

Söderström describes Spotify today as “an intelligent media service encapsulated as an agent, whether you use it directly through our application or via another agent…Spotify is now an agent that you can not only click on in our app, but talk to, ask questions of, and instruct. We can do things today that no other media services can do,” he said.

“For example, you can ask Spotify to go through your listening history song by song back to 2008, picking your true favorites, beat-stretching them by speeding them up or down, and then sorting them by key and BPM. Then you can ask it to mix them together into the perfect running playlist at your exact cadence,” Söderström explained.

Spotify has years of listening history to draw on, including the artists people return to, the songs they skip, and the music they discover. That information can help it make recommendations that feel more personal than a generic playlist generated by an AI assistant that doesn’t know much about someone’s tastes.

However, Söderström also emphasized that Spotify isn’t sending its listener data to partners. Instead, the agent asks Spotify for something, and Spotify uses its own systems to reason about the request and choose what to play.

articles.title: Spotify confirms Family Plan crackdown, but calls it a 'routine improvement' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Spotify told investors its rollout of QR code verification to ensure Family Plan members live in the same household is not a "crackdown," just a routine improvement.
articles.body:
Spotify confirmed the reports of its crackdown on Family Plan sharing during its third-quarter call with investors, calling its new method “a routine improvement” to its existing verification tools.

Over the past several days, reports had surfaced indicating that Spotify was rolling out a “QR code verification” method, where the app would prompt members on its Family Plan to verify they lived with the plan manager by scanning a QR code. This code appears on the plan manager’s phone, which the plan member then needs to scan with their own phone, according to Spotify’s support documentation .

Plan members have seven days to complete the QR code after getting a notification, which means they could be out of luck if they live outside the home and aren’t planning a return visit anytime soon. If the verification window is missed, they won’t be able to join another Family or Duo plan for 12 months, but would instead have to shift to an individual plan that they pay for themselves.

The move is meant to boost subscriptions to Spotify’s profitable Premium plans, rather than allowing adult children or friends who live apart from gaming the system to get a cheaper plan by splitting a Family Plan subscription.

During the earnings call, an investor asked a question about the crackdown and what it means, but Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström downplayed the change, calling it a “routine improvement,” not a “crackdown.”

“Family Plan has existed for a long while. It has been around for, I think it is now close to 12, 13 years in Spotify history, and it makes up a pretty significant proportion of our subscriber base,” said Norström. “As such, it is important for us to just make sure over time that we improve the verification methods that we have. There are certainly ways, over time, to find holes around it. As that happens, we figure out how to improve it over time,” he added.

The executive said that the company’s attempt to better verify its users is not something that would have an end date or would ever be complete, but would be considered an ongoing routine improvement.
